summary: A tight two-player abstract game where you race to buy irregularly-shaped patches and pack them efficiently onto your 9x9 board while managing a tiny economy of buttons and time. Turn order is driven by a shared time track rather than alternation, so tempo and timing matter as much as the puzzle itself.
praised: Elegant, tight rules that create real depth
Satisfying tactile Tetris-like puzzle of fitting patches together
Fast to teach and play, works well as a filler or gateway two-player game
Clever time-track turn order mechanism keeps both players engaged
criticised: Can feel solitaire-ish with limited direct interaction beyond patch/timing denial
Luck of the patch circle draw can swing outcomes
Limited long-term replayability once optimal patterns are learned
Only supports 2 players, excluding larger groups

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with light blocking via patch and timing denial

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: Final score is buttons remaining plus board bonuses minus empty-square penalties, so efficient patch fitting and button income dominate the outcome
